theorem eq_C_of_mahlerHom_eq_self {p : ℕ} (hp : 1 < p) {f : HahnSeries ℚ k}
    (hf : mahlerHom p (by omega) f = f) : f = HahnSeries.C (f.coeff 0)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hpQ : (1 : ℚ) < (p : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  have hp0 : (0 : ℚ) < (p : ℚ) := lt_trans zero_lt_one hpQ
  have hstep : ∀ γ : ℚ, f.coeff (γ / (p : ℚ)) = f.coeff γ := by
    intro γ
    have := congrArg (fun x : HahnSeries ℚ k => x.coeff γ) hf
    rw [coeff_mahlerHom p hp] at this
    exact this
  have hiter : ∀ (γ : ℚ) (n : ℕ), f.coeff (γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n) = f.coeff γ := by
    intro γ n
    induction n with
    | zero => simp
    | succ n ih =>
        rw [pow_succ, ← div_div, hstep, ih]
  refine HahnSeries.coeff_inj.mp (funext fun γ => ?_)
  by_cases hγ : γ = 0
  · subst hγ
    simp [HahnSeries.C_apply]
  · have hzero : f.coeff γ = 0 := by
      by_contra hne
      rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hγ with hneg | hpos
      · have hmem : ∀ n : ℕ, γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n ∈ f.support := by
          intro n
          have hppos : (0 : ℚ) < (p : ℚ) ^ n := pow_pos hp0 n
          have hco : f.coeff (γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n) = f.coeff γ := by
            have h := hiter (γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n) n
            rw [mul_div_assoc, div_self (ne_of_gt hppos), mul_one] at h
            exact h.symm
          rw [HahnSeries.mem_support, hco]
          exact hne
        have hanti : StrictAnti (fun n : ℕ => γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n) := by
          refine strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => ?_
          have hppos : (0 : ℚ) < (p : ℚ) ^ n := pow_pos hp0 n
          have hlt : γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n < 0 := mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hneg hppos
          calc γ * (p : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) = (γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n) * (p : ℚ) := by ring
            _ < (γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n) * 1 := mul_lt_mul_of_neg_left hpQ hlt
            _ = γ * (p : ℚ) ^ n := by ring
        exact (Set.isWF_iff_no_descending_seq.mp f.isWF_support _ hanti) hmem
      · have hmem : ∀ n : ℕ, γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n ∈ f.support := by
          intro n
          rw [HahnSeries.mem_support, hiter γ n]
          exact hne
        have hanti : StrictAnti (fun n : ℕ => γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n) := by
          refine strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => ?_
          have hppos : (0 : ℚ) < (p : ℚ) ^ n := pow_pos hp0 n
          have hnum : 0 < γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n := div_pos hpos hppos
          calc γ / (p : ℚ) ^ (n + 1) = (γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n) / (p : ℚ) := by
                rw [pow_succ, ← div_div]
            _ < γ / (p : ℚ) ^ n := by
                rw [div_lt_iff₀ hp0]
                nlinarith
        exact (Set.isWF_iff_no_descending_seq.mp f.isWF_support _ hanti) hmem
    simp [hzero, HahnSeries.C_apply, hγ]

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.RegularLevelSetStratification

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set

noncomputable section

/--
A well-founded algebraic category in which every nonempty object has a regular
open piece admits a finite regular stratification.  The statement is phrased
for an arbitrary predicate on subsets so that the well-founded algebraic
topology and the ambient analytic topology need not be placed on the same
type-class instance.
-/
theorem finiteRegularStratification_of_wellFounded_peel
    {Y : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace ℝ Y]
    {c : ℕ} (Algebraic : Set Y → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun T S : {Z : Set Y // Algebraic Z} => T.1 ⊂ S.1))
    (peel : ∀ S, Algebraic S → S.Nonempty →
      ∃ R : Set Y, R.Nonempty ∧ R ⊆ S ∧
        IsLocalRegularLevelSetOfCodimAtLeast R c ∧ Algebraic (S \ R)) :
    ∀ S, Algebraic S → Nonempty (FiniteRegularStratification S c) := by
  intro S hS
  let Z : {Z : Set Y // Algebraic Z} := ⟨S, hS⟩
  change Nonempty (FiniteRegularStratification Z.1 c)
  induction Z using hwf.induction with
  | h Z ih =>
      by_cases hZ : Z.1.Nonempty
      · obtain ⟨R, hRne, hRZ, hRreg, hrem⟩ := peel Z.1 Z.2 hZ
        let T : {Z : Set Y // Algebraic Z} := ⟨Z.1 \ R, hrem⟩
        have hTZ : T.1 ⊂ Z.1 := by
          refine Set.ssubset_iff_exists.mpr ⟨sdiff_subset, ?_⟩
          obtain ⟨r, hrR⟩ := hRne
          exact ⟨r, hRZ hrR, fun hrT => hrT.2 hrR⟩
        obtain ⟨tail⟩ := ih T hTZ
        have hdisj : Disjoint R T.1 := by
          rw [Set.disjoint_left]
          intro x hxR hxT
          exact hxT.2 hxR
        have hcover : Z.1 = R ∪ T.1 := by
          ext x
          constructor
          · intro hx
            by_cases hxR : x ∈ R
            · exact Or.inl hxR
            · exact Or.inr ⟨hx, hxR⟩
          · rintro (hxR | hxT)
            · exact hRZ hxR
            · exact hxT.1
        exact ⟨tail.cons hRreg hdisj hcover⟩
      · have hZempty : Z.1 = ∅ := not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hZ
        refine ⟨?_⟩
        exact {
          numberOfStrata := 0
          stratum := fun i => i.elim0
          pairwise_disjoint := by
            intro i
            exact i.elim0
          cover := by simp [hZempty]
          regular := by intro i; exact i.elim0
        }

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# Nomogenic fixed-point calibration

One periodic source word and its fixed phase quotient couple recurrent observation, nonclosed
lifted state, nonzero carry, endpoint-decoder failure, and unbounded finite-prefix history.  This is
the smallest exact calibration of the least/rational/greatest fixed-point interpretation proposed
for nomogenic fixed-point dynamics.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The length-`n` well-founded approximation to the periodic `ZMod 4` source history. -/
def nomogenicSourcePrefix (n : ℕ) : List ConstitutiveCarryMiddle :=
  List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => constitutiveCarryHistory i)

/-- The length-`n` observed approximation after quotienting the source history modulo two. -/
def nomogenicObserverPrefix (n : ℕ) : List ConstitutiveBit :=
  List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => constitutiveBaseHistory i)

@[simp] theorem nomogenicSourcePrefix_length (n : ℕ) :
    (nomogenicSourcePrefix n).length = n := by
  simp [nomogenicSourcePrefix]

@[simp] theorem nomogenicObserverPrefix_length (n : ℕ) :
    (nomogenicObserverPrefix n).length = n := by
  simp [nomogenicObserverPrefix]

/-- The observer history is the exact quotient of the source history at every time. -/
theorem nomogenicHistory_quotient (n : ℕ) :
    constitutiveCarryQuotient (constitutiveCarryHistory n) = constitutiveBaseHistory n := by
  exact constitutiveCarryQuotient_natCast n

/-- One observed period never closes the nonsplit source history. -/
theorem nomogenicSourceHistory_not_period_two (n : ℕ) :
    constitutiveCarryHistory (n + 2) ≠ constitutiveCarryHistory n := by
  rw [constitutiveCarryHistory_period_increment]
  intro h
  have h' : constitutiveCarryHistory n + constitutiveCarryInclusion 1 =
      constitutiveCarryHistory n + 0 := by simpa using h
  exact constitutiveCarryHistory_increment_ne_zero (add_left_cancel h')

/-- No pointwise decoder of the observed state reconstructs the full source trajectory. -/
theorem nomogenicHistory_no_decoder :
    ¬ ∃ d : ConstitutiveBit → ConstitutiveCarryMiddle,
      ∀ n : ℕ, d (constitutiveBaseHistory n) = constitutiveCarryHistory n := by
  rintro ⟨d, hd⟩
  have hbase := constitutiveBaseHistory_period_two 0
  have hsource : constitutiveCarryHistory (0 + 2) = constitutiveCarryHistory 0 := by
    rw [← hd (0 + 2), ← hd 0, hbase]
  exact nomogenicSourceHistory_not_period_two 0 hsource

/-- Prefix depth is unbounded even though the observed endpoint has period two. -/
theorem nomogenicSourcePrefix_unbounded (bound : ℕ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, bound < (nomogenicSourcePrefix n).length := by
  refine ⟨bound + 1, ?_⟩
  simp

/-- **Periodic producer/phase quotient/open-prefix law.**  A single source history and one declared
quotient simultaneously produce closed observer recurrence, nonzero lifted holonomy, binary carry,
failure of endpoint reconstruction, and unbounded well-founded prefix depth. -/
theorem nomogenicPeriodicProducer_phaseQuotient_recurrence_openPrefix :
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      constitutiveCarryQuotient (constitutiveCarryHistory n) = constitutiveBaseHistory n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, constitutiveBaseHistory (n + 2) = constitutiveBaseHistory n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, constitutiveCarryHistory (n + 2) =
      constitutiveCarryHistory n + constitutiveCarryInclusion 1) ∧
    constitutiveCarryInclusion 1 ≠ 0 ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, constitutiveCarryHistory (n + 2) ≠ constitutiveCarryHistory n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, constitutiveCarryHistory (n + 4) = constitutiveCarryHistory n) ∧
    (¬ ∃ d : ConstitutiveBit → ConstitutiveCarryMiddle,
      ∀ n : ℕ, d (constitutiveBaseHistory n) = constitutiveCarryHistory n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, (nomogenicSourcePrefix n).length = n) ∧
    (∀ bound : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, bound < (nomogenicSourcePrefix n).length) ∧
    (constitutiveCarrySection 1 + constitutiveCarrySection 1 -
      constitutiveCarrySection (1 + 1) = constitutiveCarryInclusion 1) := by
  exact ⟨nomogenicHistory_quotient,
    constitutiveBaseHistory_period_two,
    constitutiveCarryHistory_period_increment,
    constitutiveCarryHistory_increment_ne_zero,
    nomogenicSourceHistory_not_period_two,
    constitutiveCarryHistory_period_four,
    nomogenicHistory_no_decoder,
    nomogenicSourcePrefix_length,
    nomogenicSourcePrefix_unbounded,
    constitutiveCarry_one_one⟩

/-!
# Affine observer holonomy and the global-section field equation

Observer fibres `H v` are compared along oriented edges by unitary transports `U e` with
translation defects `b e`; an **exact global presentation** is a family `x` with
`x (tgt e) = U e (x (src e)) + b e` for every edge.

A rooted spanning-tree gauge `(A, a)` reduces the tree equations to `x v = A v (x o) + a v`, so
exact global presentations are exactly the root values solving the affine chord equations

`x − Hol e x = c e`,

whose least-squares normal operator `Δ_hol = D* D` and source current `J_src = D* c` give the
**observer field equation** `Δ_hol x = J_src` together with the separate exactness condition
`D x = c`.
-/

open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## Rooted tree gauges -/

/-- A rooted spanning-tree gauge for affine observer transport: a parent function with a
well-founded rank, the unitary transports and translation defects along tree edges, and the
resulting based transports `A v` and accumulated defects `a v`. -/
structure TreeGauge (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] {V : Type*} (H : V → Type*)
    [∀ v, NormedAddCommGroup (H v)] [∀ v, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (H v)] (o : V) where
  /-- The tree parent of a vertex. -/
  parent : V → V
  /-- A rank witnessing well-founded descent to the root. -/
  rank : V → ℕ
  /-- The root is its own parent. -/
  parent_root : parent o = o
  /-- Every non-root vertex has a parent of strictly smaller rank. -/
  rank_lt : ∀ v, v ≠ o → rank (parent v) < rank v
  /-- The unitary transport along the tree edge into `v`. -/
  U : (v : V) → (H (parent v) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] H v)
  /-- The translation defect of the tree edge into `v`. -/
  b : (v : V) → H v
  /-- The based transport from the root fibre. -/
  A : (v : V) → (H o ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] H v)
  /-- The accumulated affine defect at `v`. -/
  a : (v : V) → H v
  /-- The based transport is the identity at the root. -/
  A_root : ∀ z, A o z = z
  /-- The accumulated defect vanishes at the root. -/
  a_root : a o = 0
  /-- The based transport is built by tree composition. -/
  A_step : ∀ v, v ≠ o → ∀ z, A v z = U v (A (parent v) z)
  /-- The accumulated defect is built by affine tree composition. -/
  a_step : ∀ v, v ≠ o → a v = U v (a (parent v)) + b v

namespace TreeGauge

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {V : Type*} {H : V → Type*}
  [∀ v, NormedAddCommGroup (H v)] [∀ v, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (H v)] {o : V}
  (T : TreeGauge 𝕜 H o)

/-- The tree-edge equations of an observer family. -/
def IsTreeExact (x : ∀ v, H v) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, v ≠ o → x v = T.U v (x (T.parent v)) + T.b v

/-- The based form of a family. -/
def IsBased (x : ∀ v, H v) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, x v = T.A v (x o) + T.a v

/-- **The spanning-tree reduction.**  A family satisfies all tree-edge equations exactly when it
is the based extension of its root value. -/
theorem isTreeExact_iff_isBased (x : ∀ v, H v) : T.IsTreeExact x ↔ T.IsBased x := by
  constructor
  · intro htree v
    induction hv : T.rank v using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing v with
    | _ n ih =>
      by_cases hvo : v = o
      · subst hvo
        rw [T.A_root, T.a_root, add_zero]
      · have hpar : x (T.parent v) = T.A (T.parent v) (x o) + T.a (T.parent v) := by
          refine ih (T.rank (T.parent v)) ?_ (T.parent v) rfl
          rw [← hv]
          exact T.rank_lt v hvo
        rw [htree v hvo, hpar, map_add, ← T.A_step v hvo, T.a_step v hvo]
        abel
  · intro hbased v hvo

structure ChordData (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] {V : Type*} (H : V → Type*)

  /-- The source vertex of a chord. -/
  src : C → V
  /-- The target vertex of a chord. -/
  tgt : C → V
  /-- The unitary comparison along a chord. -/
  U : (e : C) → (H (src e) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] H (tgt e))
  /-- The translation defect of a chord. -/
  b : (e : C) → H (tgt e)

namespace ChordData

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {V : Type*} {H : V → Type*}

  ((T.A (K.src e)).trans (K.U e)).trans (T.A (K.tgt e)).symm

  (T.A (K.tgt e)).symm (K.U e (T.a (K.src e)) + K.b e - T.a (K.tgt e))

/-!
# The chain complex on an available vertex set

The recursion descends on a pair `(A, V)`: the vertices `A` forced into every face, and the vertices
`V` still available.  The complex is

```text
Δ_r^{A,V} = { S ⊆ V : S ∪ A contains no (r+1)-chain } .
```

```text
chainForcedOn N r A V          the complex
chainForcedOn_univ             Δ_r^{A,univ} = Δ_r^A
isFaceFamily_chainForcedOn     it is downward closed
faceDeletion_chainForcedOn     ** del v = Δ_r^{A, V \ {v}} **
faceLink_chainForcedOn         ** lk v  = Δ_r^{A ∪ {v}, V \ {v}} **   (for v ∈ V)
```

Both operations shrink `V` by one vertex, so the recursion of `StarReduction.lean` — which needs
only the deletion and the link — is well founded on `V.card`.  What is left is the dimension
bookkeeping: that the deletion keeps the largest face size and the link drops it by one, for the
least available vertex.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open RHTower

/-- The chain complex with forced vertices `A`, restricted to the available vertices `V`. -/
noncomputable def chainForcedOn (N r : ℕ) (A V : Finset (Fin N)) : Finset (Finset (Fin N)) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (fun S => S ⊆ V ∧ IsChainFace N r (S ∪ A))

theorem mem_chainForcedOn {N r : ℕ} {A V S : Finset (Fin N)} :
    S ∈ chainForcedOn N r A V ↔ S ⊆ V ∧ IsChainFace N r (S ∪ A) := by
  classical
  simp [chainForcedOn]

theorem isFaceFamily_chainForcedOn (N r : ℕ) (A V : Finset (Fin N)) :
    IsFaceFamily (chainForcedOn N r A V) := by
  intro S T hT hST
  rw [mem_chainForcedOn] at hT ⊢
  exact ⟨hST.trans hT.1,
    hT.2.subset (Finset.union_subset_union hST (subset_refl A))⟩

theorem chainForcedOn_univ (N r : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin N)) :
    chainForcedOn N r A Finset.univ = chainForcedFamily N r A := by
  classical
  ext S
  rw [mem_chainForcedOn, mem_chainForcedFamily]
  exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨Finset.subset_univ S, h⟩⟩

/-- **Deletion shrinks the available set.** -/
theorem faceDeletion_chainForcedOn (N r : ℕ) (A V : Finset (Fin N)) (v : Fin N) :
    faceDeletion (chainForcedOn N r A V) v = chainForcedOn N r A (V.erase v) := by
  classical
  ext S
  rw [mem_faceDeletion, mem_chainForcedOn, mem_chainForcedOn]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨⟨hSV, hface⟩, hv⟩
    exact ⟨Finset.subset_erase.mpr ⟨hSV, hv⟩, hface⟩
  · rintro ⟨hSV, hface⟩
    obtain ⟨hS, hv⟩ := Finset.subset_erase.mp hSV
    exact ⟨⟨hS, hface⟩, hv⟩

/-- **The link shrinks the available set and grows the forced set.** -/
theorem faceLink_chainForcedOn (N r : ℕ) (A V : Finset (Fin N)) {v : Fin N} (hv : v ∈ V) :
    faceLink (chainForcedOn N r A V) v = chainForcedOn N r (insert v A) (V.erase v) := by
  classical
  ext S
  rw [mem_faceLink, mem_chainForcedOn, mem_chainForcedOn, mem_chainForcedOn]
  have hins : insert v S ∪ A = S ∪ insert v A := by
    ext w
    simp only [Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_insert]
    tauto
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨⟨hSV, -⟩, hvS, ⟨-, hface⟩⟩
    rw [hins] at hface
    exact ⟨Finset.subset_erase.mpr ⟨hSV, hvS⟩, hface⟩
  · rintro ⟨hSV, hface⟩
    obtain ⟨hS, hvS⟩ := Finset.subset_erase.mp hSV
    refine ⟨⟨hS, ?_⟩, hvS, ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
    · exact hface.subset (Finset.union_subset_union (subset_refl S) (Finset.subset_insert v A))
    · exact Finset.insert_subset hv hS
    · rw [hins]
      exact hface

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# Constitutive critical-completion mechanics

This module certifies a route-independent law-generation mechanism.  Every word execution is
well-founded, but each finite executable rulebook is nonconfluent.  Its missing joining rule is
already valid in the old generated equivalence, so adjoining it is semantically conservative;
nevertheless the new executable rule produces the next marked failure.

Paper source:
`docs/drafts/pipeline/2-fully-proven/universal-law-field/endogenous-completion-mechanics/
terminating-execution-open-conservative-completion-and-critical-heredity-law.md`.
-/

namespace ConstitutiveCriticalCompletionMechanics

/-- Two-letter alphabet for the completion laboratory. -/
inductive Letter
  | a
  | b
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Finite words in the two-letter alphabet. -/
abbrev Word := List Letter

/-- Left side `a b^n a` of rule `n`. -/
def left (n : ℕ) : Word := .a :: List.replicate n .b ++ [.a]

/-- Right side `b^n a` of rule `n`. -/
def right (n : ℕ) : Word := List.replicate n .b ++ [.a]

/-- Marked overlap word for rules `m` and `n`. -/
def critical (m n : ℕ) : Word := left m ++ List.replicate n .b ++ [.a]

/-- One contextual rewrite using an indexed rule admitted by finite stage `N`. -/
def Step (N : ℕ) (u v : Word) : Prop :=
  ∃ n, 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ N ∧ ∃ p s,
    u = p ++ left n ++ s ∧ v = p ++ right n ++ s

theorem critical_eq_suffix (m n : ℕ) :
    critical m n = (.a :: List.replicate m .b) ++ left n := by
  simp [critical, left, List.append_assoc]

/-- The persistent seed rule is the first branch of the marked peak. -/
theorem critical_seed_step (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Step n (critical 1 n) (.b :: left n) := by
  refine ⟨1, by omega, hn, [], List.replicate n .b ++ [.a], ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [critical, left]
  · simp [right, left]

/-- The newest admitted rule is the second branch of the marked peak. -/
theorem critical_newest_step (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Step n (critical 1 n) (left (n + 1)) := by
  refine ⟨n, hn, le_rfl, [.a, .b], [], ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [critical_eq_suffix, left]
  · simp [left, right, List.replicate_succ]

/-- After the seed step, the newest rule reaches the other marked endpoint. -/
theorem intermediate_step (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Step n (.b :: left n) (right (n + 1)) := by
  refine ⟨n, hn, le_rfl, [.b], [], ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp
  · simp [right, List.replicate_succ]

theorem count_a_replicate_b (n : ℕ) :
    (List.replicate n Letter.b).count .a = 0 := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih => simp [List.replicate_succ, ih]

theorem count_a_left (n : ℕ) : (left n).count .a = 2 := by
  simp [left, count_a_replicate_b]

theorem count_a_right (n : ℕ) : (right n).count .a = 1 := by
  simp [right, count_a_replicate_b]

/-- Every executable rule decreases the number of `a` letters by exactly one. -/
theorem step_count_a (h : Step N u v) : v.count .a + 1 = u.count .a := by
  rcases h with ⟨n, hn, hN, p, s, rfl, rfl⟩
  rw [List.count_append, List.count_append, List.count_append, List.count_append,
    count_a_left, count_a_right]
  omega

theorem step_count_a_lt (h : Step N u v) : v.count .a < u.count .a := by
  have hcount := step_count_a h
  omega

/-- Object-level execution terminates at every finite completion stage. -/
theorem step_wellFounded (N : ℕ) :
    WellFounded (fun v u => Step N u v) := by
  apply (InvImage.wf (fun w : Word => w.count .a) (Nat.lt_wfRel.2)).mono
  intro v u h
  exact step_count_a_lt h

/-- A word is normal when it has no outgoing executable rewrite. -/
def Normal (N : ℕ) (w : Word) : Prop := ∀ v, ¬ Step N w v

theorem prefix_empty_of_left_eq (M n : ℕ) (p s : Word)
    (hp : p.count .a = 0) (h : left M = p ++ left n ++ s) : p = [] := by
  cases p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs =>
      have hx : x = .a := by
        have hh := congrArg List.head? h
        symm
        simpa [left] using hh
      subst x
      simp at hp

theorem reverse_left (n : ℕ) : (left n).reverse = left n := by
  simp [left, List.reverse_append]

/-- The right endpoint of the next missing rule is normal at stage `N`. -/
theorem normal_right_succ (N : ℕ) : Normal N (right (N + 1)) := by
  intro v h
  rcases h with ⟨n, hn, hN, p, s, hu, hv⟩
  have hc := congrArg (fun w : Word => w.count .a) hu
  simp [count_a_left, count_a_right, List.count_append] at hc
  omega

/-- The left endpoint of the next missing rule is normal at stage `N`. -/
theorem normal_left_succ (N : ℕ) : Normal N (left (N + 1)) := by
  intro v h
  rcases h with ⟨n, hn, hN, p, s, hu, hv⟩
  have hc := congrArg (fun w : Word => w.count .a) hu
  simp [count_a_left, List.count_append] at hc
  have hp : p.count .a = 0 := by omega
  have hs : s.count .a = 0 := by omega
  have hpnil : p = [] := prefix_empty_of_left_eq (N + 1) n p s hp hu
  subst p
  simp only [List.nil_append] at hu
  have hrev := congrArg List.reverse hu
  rw [reverse_left, List.reverse_append, reverse_left] at hrev
  have hsnilRev : s.reverse = [] :=

/-!
# Barycentric subdivision of affine chains

For affine chains on a real vector space, the barycentric subdivision operator is defined by the
recursion

  `Sd v = b(v) ∗ Sd (∂ v)`,

where `b(v)` is the barycenter of the vertices of `v` and `∗` is the cone operator; in degree zero
it is the identity.  The recursion is well founded because the boundary lowers the degree, and the
cone identity `∂ (b ∗ c) + b ∗ (∂ c) = c` is exactly what makes `Sd` a chain map.

The subdivision of a simplex whose vertices lie in a convex set again has all its vertices in that
convex set, since barycenters of subsets of the vertices are convex combinations of them.
-/

    ((affChainComplex R E).d 1 0).hom ((coneMap R E b 0).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)))
      = (Finsupp.single v (1 : R) : (Fin 1 → E) →₀ R)
        - Finsupp.single (fun _ : Fin 1 => b) (1 : R) := by
  rw [coneMap_single, d_single, Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  have h0 : Finsupp.single
      ((Fin.cons b v : Fin 2 → E) ∘ (0 : Fin 2).succAbove) ((-1 : R) ^ ((0 : Fin 2) : ℕ))
      = Finsupp.single v (1 : R) := by
    rw [cons_comp_succAbove_zero]
    norm_num
  have h1 : ∀ j : Fin 1, Finsupp.single
      ((Fin.cons b v : Fin 2 → E) ∘ (j.succ).succAbove) ((-1 : R) ^ ((j.succ : Fin 2) : ℕ))
      = -Finsupp.single (fun _ : Fin 1 => b) (1 : R) := by
    intro j
    have hfun : (Fin.cons b v : Fin 2 → E) ∘ (j.succ).succAbove = fun _ : Fin 1 => b := by
      funext k
      have : k = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      subst this
      simp
    rw [hfun, show ((j.succ : Fin 2) : ℕ) = 1 by simp]
    rw [← Finsupp.single_neg]
    congr 1
    norm_num
  rw [h0, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => h1 j)]
  simp [sub_eq_add_neg]

/-- The barycentric subdivision operator on affine chains. -/
noncomputable def sd : ∀ n : ℕ, (affChainComplex R E).X n ⟶ (affChainComplex R E).X n
  | 0 => 𝟙 _
  | (n + 1) => ModuleCat.ofHom (Finsupp.linearCombination R fun v : Fin (n + 2) → E =>
      (coneMap R E (bary E v) n).hom ((sd n).hom
        (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)))))

@[simp] theorem sd_zero : sd R E 0 = 𝟙 _ := rfl

theorem sd_single {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 2) → E) :
    (sd R E (n + 1)).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R))
      = (coneMap R E (bary E v) n).hom ((sd R E n).hom
          (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)))) := by
  show (Finsupp.linearCombination R fun w : Fin (n + 2) → E =>
      (coneMap R E (bary E w) n).hom ((sd R E n).hom
        (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom (Finsupp.single w (1 : R)))))
      (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)) = _
  rw [Finsupp.linearCombination_single, one_smul]

/-- **The cone identity for arbitrary chains**: `∂ (b ∗ c) + b ∗ (∂ c) = c`. -/
theorem d_coneMap_add {n : ℕ} (b : E) (c : (Fin (n + 2) → E) →₀ R) :
    ((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 2) (n + 1)).hom ((coneMap R E b (n + 1)).hom c)
      + (coneMap R E b n).hom (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom c)
      = (c : (Fin (n + 2) → E) →₀ R) := by
  have hmap : (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 2) (n + 1)).hom.comp
        (coneMap R E b (n + 1)).hom)
      + ((coneMap R E b n).hom.comp ((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom)
      = LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := (Fin (n + 2) → E) →₀ R) := by
    refine Finsupp.lhom_ext' fun v => LinearMap.ext_ring ?_
    show ((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 2) (n + 1)).hom
        ((coneMap R E b (n + 1)).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)))
      + (coneMap R E b n).hom
          (((affChainComplex R E).d (n + 1) n).hom (Finsupp.single v (1 : R)))
      = Finsupp.single v (1 : R)
    exact d_coneMap_single R E b v
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun hmap c

theorem sd_zero_apply (c : (Fin 1 → E) →₀ R) : (sd R E 0).hom c = c := rfl

/-- The augmentation of a `0`-chain: the sum of its coefficients. -/
noncomputable def aug : ((Fin 1 → E) →₀ R) →ₗ[R] R :=
  Finsupp.linearCombination R (fun _ : Fin 1 → E => (1 : R))

theorem aug_single (u : Fin 1 → E) (r : R) : aug R E (Finsupp.single u r) = r := by
  rw [aug, Finsupp.linearCombination_single, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]

/-!
# Finite monotone compatibility revision terminates

No infinite sequence can strictly add compatibility facts at every active step when the vocabulary
of possible facts is finite.  A finite monotone revision process is saturation, not open genesis.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

universe u

variable {Edge : Type u} [Fintype Edge]

/-- A finite compatibility vocabulary admits no infinite strictly increasing active history. -/
theorem constitutiveNoInfiniteStrictFiniteRevision
    (history : ℕ → Finset Edge)
    (hstep : ∀ n, history n < history (n + 1)) : False := by
  have hstrict : StrictMono history := strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ hstep
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij, heq⟩ :=
    Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite (α := ℕ) history
  exact hij (hstrict.injective heq)

/-- Every monotone finite-vocabulary history has a stable adjacent step. -/
theorem constitutiveFiniteMonotoneRevision_has_stable_step
    (history : ℕ → Finset Edge)
    (hmono : ∀ n, history n ⊆ history (n + 1)) :
    ∃ n, history n = history (n + 1) := by
  by_contra hstable
  push Not at hstable
  apply constitutiveNoInfiniteStrictFiniteRevision history
  intro n
  exact lt_of_le_of_ne (hmono n) (hstable n)

/-- Closed capstone for the finite monotone termination boundary. -/
theorem constitutiveFiniteRevisionTerminationMechanism_closed :
    (∀ history : ℕ → Finset Edge,
      (∀ n, history n < history (n + 1)) → False) ∧
    (∀ history : ℕ → Finset Edge,
      (∀ n, history n ⊆ history (n + 1)) →
        ∃ n, history n = history (n + 1)) := by
  exact ⟨constitutiveNoInfiniteStrictFiniteRevision,
    constitutiveFiniteMonotoneRevision_has_stable_step⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Placewise real/Hermitian Schur descent lowers the rank of every archimedean cone point. -/
def numberFieldArchimedeanSchur
    (A : numberFieldArchimedeanPositiveForms K (n + 1)) :
    numberFieldArchimedeanPositiveForms K n := by
  let realS := fun w : {w : InfinitePlace K // w.IsReal} =>
    matrixFirstSchur (A.1.1 w : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ)
  let complexS := fun w : {w : InfinitePlace K // w.IsComplex} =>
    matrixFirstSchur (A.1.2 w : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℂ)
  have hreal : ∀ w, (realS w).PosDef := fun w => matrixFirstSchur_posDef_real (A.2.1 w)
  have hcomplex : ∀ w, (complexS w).PosDef :=
    fun w => matrixFirstSchur_posDef_complex (A.2.2 w)
  refine ⟨(fun w => ⟨realS w, (hreal w).isHermitian⟩,
    fun w => ⟨complexS w, (hcomplex w).isHermitian⟩), ?_⟩
  exact ⟨hreal, hcomplex⟩
